doc: SSOT for the course module-description model. Read at lint time by tests/course.py, which validates every lecture module page against these rules; the human-facing pointer is course/README.md. MAGE-style: a module's shape is DATA a lint enforces, not prose a reader must remember. Add or tune a rule here and the lint applies it — no code change is needed for a new predicate of an existing rule type.

applies_to.doc: Lecture module pages only: course/lectures/act-<name>/NN-<topic>/index.md — each module is its own directory (holding index.md + slides/ + readings/), so the page is the directory index. Act landing pages (act-<name>/index.md), the calendar, and project pages are out of scope.

front_matter.doc: status is always checked against the enum. The body rules below apply in full only to a module whose description is meant to be complete (status: ready); a placeholder/draft is exempt while it is still an outline.

sessions.doc: A module that spans more than one class session declares its session titles as a front-matter block list, e.g. `sessions:` then `- "Modeling: Representation & Implementation"` — the exact strings the reference calendar's {module:...} tokens use, so each session token links to this module page (site/hooks/modules.py). The session COUNT is never declared as a separate number: it is the length of this list, and tests/course.py enforces parity with the calendar (each declared session title appears exactly once as a calendar token; the module's own title does not also appear). A module with no `sessions:` key is a single-session module.
sessions.band_doc: Prose budget for a ready module description, per session: body words (everything after the front matter, whitespace-split) should land in sessions x 750 .. sessions x 1000 — 750-1,000 for a one-session module, 1,500-2,000 for a two-session module. Checked audit-only by tests/course.py (check_course_lander_prose_word_band) while existing landers are out of band.

rules.message: A ready module must open with a **Premise.** line whose thesis is a single *italicized* sentence — e.g. `**Premise.** *The engineered medium affects the engineering process.*`
A ready module needs a short framing paragraph between the **Premise.** line and the first `##` section — the description is not a bare premise.
A ready module description is sectioned with `##` headings, not a single one-liner.
A ready module must develop its model as a list of >=2 items, each led by a **bold** statement or an *italic* question (the dimensions or levels the module teaches).
The one-line `**Concepts.** …` form is the outline placeholder; a `status: ready` module carries a full Premise+model description instead.
